messages.author: 4f3a6f412f9a536b
messages.subject: Issue with data quality?
parts:
I'm wondering about an issue I'm having with data quality. I seem to be able to analyze the data in ActiLife with an appropriate output, but when I try to analyze the .gt3x file with GGIR, I get the following error in part 1:

"Extract signal features (metrics) with the g.getmeta function:
Loading chunk: 1 2Error in data[, c("x", "y", "z")] : subscript out of bounds"

As such, there isn't even anything in the QC folder to try to better understand the issue.

Any help you might be able to provide would be very welcome. Searched for this error, and I couldn't find it anywhere.

Thanks!

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Issue with data quality?
parts:
Hi Peter,

This is a bug I fixed a few minutes ago. It was introduced in release 3.0-6 and is specific to ActiGraph with idle sleep mode turned on or custom csv format data with time gaps.

To try out my fix you can install the test version of GGIR with:
install.packages("remotes")
library("remotes')
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue1104_merging_imputed_timegap_data")

Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Issue with data quality?
parts:
You cannot process ActiGraph count data as if it is raw data. You need different input parameters for that to work as detailed in the GGIR documentation:
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter2_Pipeline.html#input-files

Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Issue with data quality?
parts:
Hi Yiling,
Can you read the file with read.gt3x?

library(read.gt3x)
data = read.gt3x("yourfile.gt3x", batch_begin = 1, batch_end = 2)
print(data)

If not, then the problem is with the data itself, which somehow is in a format that package read.gt3x cannot handle.
If yes, then the problem is with GGIR and it would be good to have a copy of the file to investigate.

Thanks,
Vincent
